claims.text: Language models demonstrate quantitative improvement with increasing scale.
Language models demonstrate new qualitative capabilities with increasing scale.
Language model performance improves with model scale.
Language model calibration improves with model scale.
Language model performance and calibration are poor in absolute terms.
Language model performance and calibration are poor compared to human expert rater performance.
Performance is remarkably similar across different language model classes.
Sparse transformer architectures provide performance benefits over dense architectures.
Tasks that improve gradually and predictably with scale commonly involve a large knowledge or memorization component.
Tasks that exhibit breakthrough behavior at a critical scale often involve multiple steps, multiple components, or brittle metrics.
Social bias typically increases with scale in language model settings with ambiguous context.
Social bias increases in language models with scale can be improved with prompting.

evidence.description: Language models demonstrate both quantitative improvement and new qualitative capabilities with increasing scale.
Language models demonstrate both quantitative improvement and new qualitative capabilities with increasing scale.
Findings include: model performance and calibration both improve with scale...
Findings include: model performance and calibration both improve with scale...

...social bias typically increases with scale in settings with ambiguous context...
...but this can be improved with prompting.

methodologies.name: BIG-bench Evaluation Framework
methodologies.description: Evaluated language model capabilities and behaviors across 204 diverse tasks spanning millions to hundreds of billions of parameters.
conditions: Model sizes spanning millions to hundreds of billions of parameters

limitations.text: Present and near-future capabilities and limitations of language models are poorly characterized.
Language model performance and calibration are poor in absolute terms and when compared with human expert raters.
Social bias typically increases with scale in settings with ambiguous context.
